head_commit.message: [Issue #7657] Upgrade APIFlask to 3.1 (#8175) ## Summary Fixes #7657 ## Changes proposed * Upgrade to APIFlask 3.0.x * Cleanup how we setup auth now that the approach can be done a bit simpler with new version of equivalent classes ## Context for reviewers We can remove quite a bit of boilerplate for our auth - no longer needing security schemes as MultiAuth is fully supported automatically. This does mean any endpoint that uses 2 types of auth required a slight adjustment to the definition, but no functionality should actually change with this. There were a handful of endpoints using an alternative approach to auth for JWT + User API Key as we built 2 similar things around the same time, I removed the duplicate that was clunkier to use in favor of the simpler common one. ## Validation steps Relying on the unit tests + e2e tests to verify I didn't fundamentally break auth which is where most changes are. Only changed a few tests that switched auth slightly (just text changing). The main thing I needed to manually check is that our OpenAPI docs work correctly. The reason we previously had to specify the schemes on every API was otherwise the auth wouldn't connect properly for multi auth. All of the endpoints locally have auth still viewable without issue - the info is properly connected to every endpoint automatically.

head_commit.message:
[Issue #9202] Replace localstack with s3mock + elasticmq (#9370)

## Summary
Fixes #9202

## Changes proposed
* Replace localstack with s3mock + elasticmq

## Context for reviewers
Localstack community edition is going away -
https://blog.localstack.cloud/the-road-ahead-for-localstack - we
temporarily worked around this problem by statically defining the image
we use, but that was always temporary.

While I considered using
[moto](https://docs.getmoto.org/en/latest/docs/server_mode.html) - they
do not have any way to persist data if you stop and start containers, a
feature we really want for at least s3.

Instead I found s3mock + elasticmq which conveniently both have a way to
configure s3 buckets / sqs queues to be created for you, letting us
remove the create script we had before.

Because we've had issues before with disk space in our github actions, I
verified how large the images are.
* `localstack` - 1.8gb
* `s3mock` - 230mb
* `elasticmq` - 131mb

So this should give us more leeway there.

## Validation steps
Don't have 100% exact step-by-step instructions, you can check it out
and try running the commands. `make init` should be all you need to do
to get this stood up. Just giving a checklist of what I checked.

---

Verified CI/CD works - e2e tests use the s3 setup.

Verified that I could use the AWS cli to interact with the s3 bucket +
sqs queue - added a few of these commands to the docs.

Verified that the seed script is able to load data (many things load
data to s3).

Verified via the frontend (and thus also our APIs) that files could be
fetched/uploaded for:
* Opportunity attachments on the opportunity page / GET opp endpoint
* Can upload attachments to an application
* Can fetch an application submission after that is generated on the
application page

The above means it works for both our draft and public bucket, although
locally those behave identically since there is no CDN, although the
logic branches a bit before converging.

---

For SQS, we only have one usage of it, I was able to send events via the
workflow event API, and the service was able to pull from them.

head_commit.message:
[Issue #8768] Create endpoint for paginated workflow audit event (#9374)

## Summary

Fixes #8768  

## Changes proposed

Create POST /v1/workflows/:workflow_id/audit - this endpoint will return
a paginated list of audit events about a given workflow.

## Context for reviewers

Request and response schemas can be found at the ticket summary:
https://github.com/HHS/simpler-grants-gov/issues/8768

AuthZ
Allows JWT or user API key
The same as what we implemented in the GET workflow endpoint
https://github.com/HHS/simpler-grants-gov/issues/8107


Logic

- Fetch the workflow, 404 if not found
- Enforce AuthZ (same as GET workflow endpoint), 403 if not authorized
- Using our pagination utils, construct a request, and return a
paginated response

## Validation steps

- Endpoint created
- Tests added that verify audit events can be returned with pagination

---------

Co-authored-by: Hao Wang <hao.wang@reisystems.com>
